summary: Phase 149O.1I -- HATP Verification Engine Implementation (Wave 4): implemented the Wave-4 HATP proof verification engine per the 149O.1D plan's explicit Module Ownership Proposal (Sec 7), which co-locates the verifier (subsystem I) and substrate-readiness gate (subsystem J) inside src/pcae/core/human_approval_trusted_provenance.py alongside Wave 3 -- the one plan-sanctioned exception to the otherwise Wave-3-only file boundary nine historical test assertions previously enforced (narrowed, not deleted, to their original intent: no RAE/Permission-Broker/agent coupling). Added HATPVerificationStatus, an Enum reproducing HATP-REQ-078's closed 13-state vocabulary verbatim (VALID, MISSING, MALFORMED, INVALID_SIGNATURE, UNKNOWN_SIGNER, UNAUTHORIZED_SIGNER, REVOKED_SIGNER, INVALID_ATTESTATION, USER_PRESENCE_NOT_PROVEN, WRONG_OPERATION, WRONG_REPOSITORY, WRONG_DEPLOYMENT, EXPIRED), independently confirmed disjoint from the Permission Broker (ALLOW/DENY/HUMAN_REVIEW) and RAE-001 vocabularies. Added the immutable HATPVerificationResult (status + non-secret reasons only -- no approved/authorized/approval_present/can_execute/permission field anywhere in the Wave-4 API, independently field-set-tested). Added verify_hatp_proof, which consumes: the Wave-3 HumanApprovalProvenanceProof; the Wave-3 canonical signed payload via canonicalize_hatp_proof_payload (called directly, never rebuilt independently); the read-only Wave-2 HATPTrustStore (via its existing lookup_signer/lookup_principal/lookup_authority/resolve_deployment_authorization/environment_status methods -- no new write method, hatp_bootstrap.py byte-unchanged); a new provider-neutral HATPProofVerifierProvider interface; an explicit HATPExpectedOperation (the concrete operation the caller is authorizing, compared by value against the proof's own fields to reject WRONG_OPERATION replay -- HATP-REQ-069/071/083); and an explicit evaluation_time (never datetime.now() internally, keeping verification a pure, replayable function of its inputs). Signer trust always resolves through the protected registry, never proof self-assertion (HATP-REQ-077): proof.principal_id/proof.provider_profile are cross-checked against the registry's SignerRecord for the exact signer_key_id, with mismatch resolving to UNKNOWN_SIGNER/UNAUTHORIZED_SIGNER respectively. A documented, deterministic (non-normative -- HATP-REQ-079 states the success conjunction as an unordered AND-list, not a mandated failure order) fail-closed check sequence covers: missing/malformed proof, genuinely-missing trust store (HATP-REQ-042, mapped to MISSING, distinguished from a merely-unenrolled signer via environment_status().status==UNAVAILABLE), unknown/revoked signer, provider-profile mismatch, provider exception or unrecognized provider result (fail-closed to INVALID_SIGNATURE), invalid signature, unproven human presence, invalid attestation, inactive principal/authority, repository/deployment mismatch (WRONG_REPOSITORY/WRONG_DEPLOYMENT, reusing the existing Wave-2 deployment_binding_matches strict Layer-1+Layer-2 helper, no independent 'looks equal' shortcut), operation-identity mismatch (WRONG_OPERATION), and future-dated issued_at beyond a documented 60-second clock-skew tolerance (EXPIRED, HATP-REQ-085). Any HATPTrustStoreError raised at any point is caught and resolves to MISSING, never propagated. Added inspect_hatp_verification_substrate_readiness, which inspects the 149O.1D plan Sec 9 seven-term activation conjunction and mechanically forces operational=False in this wave via a hardcoded, internally-asserted provider_profile_available=False/provider_attestation_trusted=False (no real hardware provider exists until Wave 5) -- independently re-tested from outside the module that this can never return True, and that the function takes no provider argument at all (so no caller can influence it). HATPVerificationSubstrateStatus has exactly one member, NOT_READY -- no READY member exists for this wave to accidentally return. This function is deliberately separate from verify_hatp_proof (a legitimate proof must be able to reach VALID in a controlled test context per HATP-001's own attack #20, even though the broader deployment substrate is not production-safe -- conflating the two would make attack #20 unreachable by construction). Added new module src/pcae/core/hatp_providers.py: HATPProviderVerificationOutcome (signature_valid/human_presence_proven/attestation_valid, no authorization field), the HATPProofVerifierProvider Protocol, and TestHATPProofVerifierProvider -- a deterministic, explicitly non-production test provider (HATP-REQ-022) whose sign() test-fixture helper produces a SHA-256-based fake assertion bound to the exact canonical payload bytes + signer + profile, giving every mutation/replay test genuine byte-exact sensitivity without any real cryptography; never imported by human_approval_trusted_provenance.py (source-scanned), and structurally unreachable from any production configuration (no registration mechanism, no env var, no CLI flag). No new hardware/crypto dependency added to pyproject.toml. New suite tests/test_hatp_verification_engine.py: 59 passed, covering vocabulary exhaustiveness/disjointness, result-type field-set purity, the canonical-byte boundary (provider receives exact canonicalize_hatp_proof_payload(proof) bytes), the positive canonical control (valid fixture -> VALID), every individual failure condition with its specific root cause, provider-exception/unknown-result fail-closed, the full signed-field mutation matrix (repository_id, decision_record_id/digest, binding_id/digest, principal_id, signer_key_id, provider_profile, issued_at -- each verified against its actual resulting status, since three of these fields are caught by an earlier registry cross-check rather than signature invalidation, which is a stronger guarantee, not a weaker one), AG3/AG5 individual field mutation, timestamp mutation (.001->.002 invalidates), equivalent-timestamp-syntax (Z vs +00:00 produces identical canonical bytes and verifies identically -- correct, not a bypass), determinism across repeated calls, test-provider-cannot-activate-production, no-approval-derivation source scan, no-production-call-site scan across rollback_approval_evidence.py/permission_broker*.py/agent.py, bidirectional dependency-direction audit, no-secret-material-in-diagnostics, and provider-Protocol runtime-conformance. Registered in Fast Green (deterministic, sub-100ms, no subprocess). Nine historical Wave-3-purity-boundary test assertions across test_phase_149o_1g/1h/1h_2/1h_4/1h_6 that forbade any hatp_bootstrap import into human_approval_trusted_provenance.py were updated in-line, each documented with the specific plan/requirement citation justifying the narrowing to the module's actual, still-narrow boundary (no RAE/Permission-Broker/agent coupling). Two historical live-working-tree self-checks (test_phase_149o_1d and test_phase_149o_1h_6, both of which asserted 'no uncommitted src/pcae/ change right now' -- true only during their own originating phase and structurally unrenewable afterward, since no base-commit reference was ever recorded) were retired to documented pytest.skip() no-ops rather than deleted, preserving discoverability. Full regression: Wave-1/2 (test_repository_identity + test_hatp_bootstrap_foundation + test_phase_149o_1e/1f/1f_1) 103 passed; 149O.1F.2 90 passed; combined Wave-3 + 149O.1H family + new Wave-4 suite 990 passed / 1 skipped; report-trust (test_phase_reports + test_phase_reports_cli + test_phase_report_trust_hard_fail + test_push_phase_report_identity_137f1) 201 passed, exact match; HATP contract/plan (test_phase_149o_1c + test_phase_149o_1d) 126 passed / 1 skipped, 127 total matching prior exactly; RAE canonical-provenance suite run directly 4 failed / 13 passed (same 4 known pre-existing B-149O-1..4 forgery findings already OPEN, unaffected); Permission Broker suites (test_permission_broker + test_permission_broker_foundation) 295 passed; RAE model/contract/validation/persistence suites 77 passed; test_agent.py full run confirmed no new failures (agent module unmodified, zero call sites into it); Permission-Broker consumer-scope-inventory shows the same pre-existing false-positive already present via hatp_bootstrap.py's own docstring prose before this phase (unaffected, unrelated to this phase's changes); Fast Green (-m fast_green -n auto) 4590 passed, exactly 4531 entering baseline + 59 new Wave-4 tests, zero regression. Files changed this phase: src/pcae/core/human_approval_trusted_provenance.py (append-only Wave-4 addition + new top-of-file imports, no existing Wave-3 symbol modified), src/pcae/core/hatp_providers.py (new), tests/test_hatp_verification_engine.py (new, 59 tests), tests/conftest.py (Fast Green registration), nine historical HATP test files (narrowed purity-boundary assertions + two retired self-checks + two allowed-file-widening entries), docs/PHASE_149O_1I_HATP_VERIFICATION_ENGINE_IMPLEMENTATION.md (new), PROJECT_STATUS.md, CHANGELOG.md, plus task-lifecycle files -- zero files under src/pcae/core/hatp_bootstrap.py, src/pcae/core/repository_identity.py, src/pcae/core/rollback_approval_evidence.py, src/pcae/core/permission_broker*.py, src/pcae/core/agent.py, src/pcae/commands/agent.py, or docs/contracts/ changed (independently git-diff-confirmed and source-scan-confirmed). No verify_hatp_proof or inspect_hatp_verification_substrate_readiness call site exists anywhere outside this module and its own test suite. HATP WAVE 4 VERIFICATION ENGINE IMPLEMENTED -- READY FOR INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION. HATP PRODUCTION: NOT READY (unchanged -- still absent: real hardware signer, real device attestation, Class-B OS deployment provisioning, RAE/HATP production integration, AG3/AG5 Permission Broker wiring, approval_present=True derivation). validation_results.name: closed_vocabulary_exact_match

validation_results.name: no_boolean_verification_api
validation_results.result: HATPVerificationResult exposes only status (13-state enum) + reasons (diagnostics tuple) -- never a bare True/False; every distinct failure cause (cryptographic, unknown signer, unauthorized signer, wrong repository, unsupported version-defensive, attestation failure, human-presence failure) maps to a distinct status.

validation_results.name: verification_result_not_approval
validation_results.result: Field-set equality assertion: HATPVerificationResult fields == {status, reasons} exactly; forbidden set {approved, authorized, approval_present, can_execute, permission, valid, trusted} disjoint from it. Same check applied to HATPProviderVerificationOutcome.

validation_results.name: fail_closed_default
validation_results.result: Provider exception, unrecognized provider return value, and trust-store exception at any lookup point all resolve to an explicit non-VALID status (INVALID_SIGNATURE / MISSING respectively), never propagate, never VALID.

validation_results.name: input_type_boundary
validation_results.result: verify_hatp_proof's primary input is the typed Wave-3 HumanApprovalProvenanceProof, not a raw dict; a non-instance input (including None) resolves to MISSING/MALFORMED, never parsed independently.

validation_results.name: canonical_signed_payload_boundary
validation_results.result: Provider receives canonicalize_hatp_proof_payload(proof) bytes directly (imported, called, never independently reconstructed); byte-level test confirms exact equality between provider-received bytes and this function's output.

validation_results.name: signature_verification_boundary_and_provider_neutral_architecture
validation_results.result: HATPProofVerifierProvider Protocol defined with a single provider-neutral verify() method; no FIDO2/PIV/WebAuthn/YubiKey-specific import or logic anywhere in hatp_providers.py or human_approval_trusted_provenance.py; no new hardware/crypto dependency in pyproject.toml.

validation_results.name: test_provider_containment
validation_results.result: TestHATPProofVerifierProvider never referenced by human_approval_trusted_provenance.py (source-scanned); inspect_hatp_verification_substrate_readiness takes no provider parameter at all; a VALID per-proof result via the test provider does not change substrate readiness (still operational=False).

validation_results.name: trust_store_dependency_single_authority
validation_results.result: verify_hatp_proof consumes only HATPTrustStore's existing read-only methods (lookup_signer, lookup_principal, lookup_authority, resolve_deployment_authorization, environment_status) and the existing deployment_binding_matches helper -- no registry parsing, ownership check, or duplicate handling reimplemented. hatp_bootstrap.py byte-unchanged (git diff empty).

validation_results.name: signer_and_provider_self_selection_defense
validation_results.result: proof.principal_id and proof.provider_profile are cross-checked against the registry's SignerRecord for signer_key_id; a mismatch resolves to UNKNOWN_SIGNER/UNAUTHORIZED_SIGNER, never trusted from the proof alone (HATP-REQ-077). Deployment binding's own principal_id/signer_key_id/provider_profile must also agree (WRONG_DEPLOYMENT on mismatch).

validation_results.name: revocation_and_authority_at_consumption_time
validation_results.result: Signer revocation and principal/authority active-status are checked against the live trust store at verification time (HATP-REQ-088), not cached from proof-creation time.

validation_results.name: individual_failure_condition_tests
validation_results.result: Dedicated tests for INVALID_SIGNATURE, UNKNOWN_SIGNER, UNAUTHORIZED_SIGNER (3 root causes: inactive principal, no authority record, wrong provider profile), REVOKED_SIGNER, WRONG_REPOSITORY, WRONG_DEPLOYMENT (3 root causes: no binding, wrong root, same-ID-wrong-deployment), USER_PRESENCE_NOT_PROVEN, INVALID_ATTESTATION, MISSING (2 root causes: no proof, no trust store), MALFORMED (2 root causes: not a proof instance, defensive unsupported-version bypass), WRONG_OPERATION (3 root causes: different decision, different AG3 job, different family), EXPIRED (future-dated beyond 60s tolerance). All pass with the expected exact status.

validation_results.name: proof_mutation_matrix
validation_results.result: Every signed field (repository_id, decision_record_id/digest, binding_id/digest, principal_id, signer_key_id, provider_profile, issued_at) individually mutated against previously-produced evidence: all invalidate (either INVALID_SIGNATURE via changed canonical bytes, or an even-earlier registry cross-check status for the three identity-binding fields). AG3 (job_id, original_commit_sha) and AG5 (per_id, ecp_id) operation-reference fields individually mutated: both invalidate.

validation_results.name: timestamp_mutation_and_equivalence
validation_results.result: .001Z -> .002Z with old evidence invalidates (INVALID_SIGNATURE). Z vs +00:00 representations of the same instant produce byte-identical canonical payloads and verify identically under the same evidence -- confirmed correct (signatures bind canonical semantic payloads, not lexical spelling), not a bypass.

validation_results.name: determinism
validation_results.result: Repeated verify_hatp_proof calls with identical inputs produce identical results (5 repetitions, single distinct result in the set); evaluation_time is always caller-supplied, never datetime.now() internally (source-scanned, docstring-excluded).

validation_results.name: unsupported_version_defensive
validation_results.result: Structurally unreachable through normal Wave-3 construction; exercised via copy.copy + object.__setattr__ bypass of __post_init__ to prove the defensive guard inside verify_hatp_proof itself, independent of Wave-3's own guard. Resolves MALFORMED.
